parts.t: Neighbourhood guide · City of Surrey · Cloverdale

Serpentine is a rural MLS® area south and west of the Cloverdale town centre, reaching roughly from Highway 99 east to the Langley border at 196 Street, and from about 32 Avenue north to 52 Avenue. The edges are approximate. Homes here are mostly acreages and farms, with many on low land along the Nicomekl River. On rural land, ALR status, water, septic and flooding matter as much as the house.

Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 13, 2026. I have worked in Fraser Valley real estate since 2015. Rules and boundaries change, so confirm anything important with the City of Surrey and the Agricultural Land Commission.
Not legal, planning or financial advice. Confirm zoning, plan designations and school catchments before you buy or sell.
Send me the address and I’ll check its zoning, ALR status and anything that could affect value before you write an offer.

Serpentine is one of Surrey’s most desirable acreage communities, known for large estate properties, farmland, and private rural settings. Homes in Serpentine often feature expansive lots, agricultural land, custom-built residences, and long-term investment potential.
This page displays live MLS® listings updated daily, including new acreage listings, estate homes, and development opportunities in the Serpentine area.

Buyers are drawn to Serpentine for privacy, land value, and proximity to major commuter routes while still maintaining a country atmosphere. If you’re considering buying or selling acreage in this area, understanding zoning, ALR regulations, and land value trends is critical.

blocks.text: Planning and the ALR in Serpentine

parts.t: No City plan is named for Serpentine, so check zoning, ALR status and flood rules for the exact property.
Much of the Serpentine and Nicomekl lowland is close to sea level and was once an intertidal zone. Farmers began dyking it in the late 1800s.
Surrey restricts new development in the 200-year floodplain of both rivers, with exceptions for existing zoning and approved plans.

Check the ALC map and ask the City of Surrey what the property is zoned and what that allows.
Ask the City whether the land is in the floodplain and what that means for building, and get an insurance quote before you remove subjects (the conditions in your offer).
If the home is on a well, get a flow test and a water quality test.
Find out the system’s age and service history, and have it inspected.
Ask whether barns, shops and suites were built with permits.
Look for covenants, rights of way and easements, including drainage rights of way.

Serpentine is an MLS® area name for rural land south of the Cloverdale town centre in Surrey. On the MLS® map its edges are roughly 52 to 54 Avenue on the north, 196 Street (the Langley border) on the east, 32 Avenue on the south (40 Avenue west of 168 Street), and about 144 to 148 Street near Highway 99 on the west. These edges are approximate and are not an official City boundary, so ask me if a specific address is in it.
